item.title: Former OpenAI Staffers Warn That xAI’s Poor Safety Record Could Complicate SpaceX’s IPO
item.description: The ex-employees, who cofounded a new AI watchdog group, say investors deserve more information about xAI’s safety practices before SpaceX goes public.

item.title: Tom Steyer Wants to Save California From Billionaires. But Also Doesn’t Want Them to Leave
item.description: The hedge fund billionaire turned gubernatorial candidate wants to tax California’s ultrawealthy, regulate AI, and keep Silicon Valley happy at the same time. Good luck with that.

item.title: Elon Musk Loses Landmark Lawsuit Against OpenAI
item.description: The nine-member panel took only two hours to return a verdict in favor of OpenAI on Monday, which the judge quickly adopted as her own final decision.

item.title: I’m a Normie. Can Normies Really Vibe Code?
item.description: Apparently anyone can vibe code anything these days. So Claude and I tried to make a database for tracking the petty grievances of the masses.

item.title: Some Asexuals Are Using AI Companions for Intimacy Without the Sex
item.description: “I’ve got one hand on the keyboard, one hand down below,” an artist who role-plays with their chatbot tells WIRED. But some asexual advocates aren’t thrilled about the association.

item.title: Greg Brockman Officially Takes Control of OpenAI’s Products in Latest Shake-Up
item.description: OpenAI is once again reorganizing its executive ranks as part of its effort to unify ChatGPT and Codex into one core product experience.

item.title: Mira Murati Wants Her AI to ‘Keep Humans in the Loop’
item.description: The Thinking Machines Lab founder and former CTO of OpenAI tells WIRED she isn’t interested in automating people out of jobs. Instead, she’s building AI that can collaborate.

item.title: The Real Losers of the Musk v. Altman Trial
item.description: A federal jury is now deciding whether Elon Musk will win his lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman—but the trial has made everyone look bad.

item.title: An Engineer’s Post Protesting Laptop Surveillance Is Going Viral Inside Meta
item.description: Meta employees in the US and UK are organizing against corporate software that tracks workers’ keystrokes and mouse activity.

item.title: Trump’s Tech Posse in China, Who’s Winning in Musk v. Altman, and Hantavirus Conspiracy Theories
item.description: Today on Uncanny Valley, we discuss how Donald Trump’s visit to China could influence conversations between world leaders at a moment when the economic and foreign policy stakes couldn’t be higher.
